fullPassage: The idea of music direction, in the sense of someone shaping and leading a musical performance, goes back to the beginnings of music. Even the gamelans of ancient Indonesia had leaders who would signal to the group changes of meter and tempo, beginnings and endings, and transitions from piece to piece. Yet listening audiences are not always essential for a performance to be meaningful, and for good aesthetic reason. They need not be aware to fulfill their experience; indeed, the unnecessarily conspicuous presence of a musical leader will detract from it. An audience is better off, for the most part, taking in the whole of a stage work rather than being party to the techniques that go into realizing it. This is not to say that when an orchestra plays alone the audience members' eyes are not fixed on the conductor for the majority of the time; they probably are. When music is accompanying something happening on stage, however, all eyes turn to the stage, and so do everyone's ears, too (including the music director's).

det.analysis: conspicuous(형용사)를 수식하려면 부사가 필요하고, 문맥상 '불필요하게' 눈에 띄는 존재감이므로 접두사 un- + 부사어미 -ly를 붙여 unnecessarily로 변환

overlay.excerptSentences: They need not be aware to fulfill their experience; indeed, the __________ (necessary) conspicuous presence of a musical leader will detract from it.

questions.passage: The idea of music direction, in the sense of someone shaping and leading a musical performance, goes back to the beginnings of music. Even the gamelans of ancient Indonesia had leaders who would signal to the group changes of meter and tempo, beginnings and endings, and transitions from piece to piece. Yet listening audiences are not always essential for a performance to be meaningful, and for good aesthetic reason. They need not be aware to fulfill their experience; indeed, the unnecessarily conspicuous presence of a musical leader will detract from it. An audience is better off, for the most part, taking in the whole of a stage work rather than being party to the __________. This is not to say that when an orchestra plays alone the audience members' eyes are not fixed on the conductor for the majority of the time; they probably are. When music is accompanying something happening on stage, however, all eyes turn to the stage, and so do everyone's ears, too (including the music director's).
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 관객은 무대 작품의 전체를 받아들이는 편이 __에 관여하는 것보다 낫다
det.analysis:
❌ ① emotions that arise from watching: '감정'은 기법이 아님
❌ ② instruments used on stage: '악기'는 기법이 아님
❌ ③ historical background of the composer: '작곡가 배경'은 맥락과 무관
✅ ④ techniques that go into realizing it: '실현하는 기법'은 원문과 일치 ← 정답
det.tip: techniques that go into realizing it = 작품을 실현하는 데 필요한 기법

Even the gamelans of ancient Indonesia had leaders who would signal to the group changes of meter and tempo, beginnings and endings, and transitions from piece to piece. Yet listening audiences are not always essential for a performance to be meaningful, and for good aesthetic reason. They need not be aware to fulfill their experience; indeed, the unnecessarily conspicuous presence of a musical leader will detract from it. An audience is better off, for the most part, taking in the whole of a stage work rather than being party to the techniques that go into realizing it. det.korean: 무대에서 무언가가 일어날 때 모든 시선이 무대를 향하고, ____도 마찬가지다
det.analysis:
❌ ① the conductor takes a bow: '지휘자가 인사하다'는 공연 종료 맥락이지 수반 상황이 아님
❌ ② the musicians stop playing: '연주가 멈추다'는 원문과 반대
✅ ③ so do everyone's ears, too: '모든 사람의 귀도 마찬가지'는 원문과 일치 ← 정답
❌ ④ the audience members leave the hall: '관객이 떠나다'는 맥락과 무관
det.tip: 시선(eyes) + 청각(ears) 모두 무대로 향한다. 도치 구문 so do ~
